title: SRE runbook draft — rate limiting, quota abuse, and leaked API keys
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working draft runbook and post-incident notes focused on three related classes of incidents we keep seeing: traffic floods (sudden spikes causing quota exhaustion), leaked API keys being used from multiple geos/ASNs, and WAF rules required to block abuse without disrupting legitimate traffic. Intended audience: first-line on-call, SREs, and SEs who own API surface rate limiting and quota enforcement.

TL;DR (for pagers):
- Detect: 5xx rate > 3% for 10m OR token consumption > 3x baseline sustained for 5m OR unique client_keys > 20x baseline in 15m.
- Mitigate immediate impact: apply global emergency throttling policy (emergency-token-bucket=100r/s), revoke or rotate compromised keys, and enable emergency WAF rule set.
- Follow-up: open postmortem ticket (JIRA:SRE-4123), collect KV cache traces, update quota/error dashboards, run replays to validate false-positive rate.

Detection signals and alerting (detailed):
- Metrics to watch (alert thresholds are suggestions):
  * per-route 5xx rate: alert if > 3% for 10 min (critical)
  * per-customer token rate: alert if > 3x rolling 7d p50 for 5 min (warning -> escalate)
  * new-client-key spike: alert when new distinct API keys active in 15m > 20x baseline
  * geo/ASN convergence: if >50% of requests for a customer come from one ASN not seen historically, tag as suspicious
  * WAF blocked ratio: alert if WAF blocks suddenly > 10% and 2xx drops > 5%
  * queue depth on inference workers: alert if queue depth > 200 per worker pool for 1m
  * cost burn: billing anomaly if tokens/sec cost > forecast by 50% for 30m

- Signal sources: Prometheus (runtime + routing), ELK (request logs), CDN logs (edge-level spikes), infra billing metrics, WAF logs. Correlate using the incident playbook query set (see linked Confluence).

First-response playbook (step-by-step):
1) Triage (0-5 min):
   - Confirm anomaly using prometheus: query top-10 routes by token/sec and error rates.
   - Check request auth distribution: top client_key(s) and count distinct IPs and ASNs.
   - Post a short note in #oncall-rotation with discovered facts.

2) Emergency mitigation (5-20 min):
   - If blasting traffic across many keys: raise global emergency throttle: PATCH /admin/throttle?policy=emergency-global-100r  (ops-only endpoint).
   - If one or few keys are responsible: rotate/revoke keys for impacted customer(s). Command: POST /admin/keys/revoke {key_id: <key>} (requires 2-person approval if customer is prod-critical).
   - If attack looks like a low-quality flood (many IPs, same ASN) enable WAF blocking rule set: toggle via console -> security -> waf -> "emergency-block-mode". Record change id.
   - If quota exhaustion: temporarily increase capacity for Dedicated pools (if contractual) or enable degraded model fallback for hosted API routes. Endpoint: /admin/pools/scale?policy=burst-allow

3) Stabilize (20-60 min):
   - Work with Solutions Eng/Product to communicate to customers impacted by revocations/throttles. Use /ops/send-customer-incident to draft messages.
   - Start sampling offending requests (log sample rate 100%) and capture full headers for investigation (retention note: redact PII before sharing).
   - If WAF rule created, validate false positives on a sampled subset; roll back if >2% legitimate traffic impacted.

4) Escalation (if not stabilized in 60m):
   - Page SRE lead and Oncall coverage from Eng infra. Consider region-level routing to healthy regions.
   - If suspected key leakage across many customers, notify Security and start account compromise playbook: CONFLUENCE:security/key-leak-playbook.

5) Recovery & cleanup (post-stabilization):
   - Revoke any emergency throttles and revert temporary WAF rules only after 2h stable with normal traffic patterns.
   - Rotate any keys that were suspected even if not revoked earlier; notify owners and provide new keys with short TTL.
   - Re-enable normal telemetry sampling.

Runbook snippets and useful commands (copyable):
- Prometheus top token rate: topk(10, sum by(route) (rate(tokens_total[1m])))
- Distinct keys in logs (elk): count(distinct(client_key)) by 15m
- Revoke key (ops CLI): opsctl keys revoke --key <KEY_ID> --reason "suspected-leak-sre"
- Enable emergency throttle (ops CLI): opsctl throttle apply --name emergency-global-100r --limit 100r/s --scope global --comment "oncall emergency"
- WAF toggle (console UI / API): POST /api/waf/rulesets/{id}/activate?mode=block&reason="sre-emergency"

On-call notes (real incident sketch — for context and examples):
- 2026-02-28 14:03 UTC: Pager triggered (alerts: high token/sec, rising 5xx). Oncall: Priya Kaur.
- 14:05: quick triage: top route /v1/generate showing 30x token rate; top key K-89ab used from 3500 IPs across 4 ASNs.
- 14:10: enabled emergency-global-100r throttle. 14:12: 5xx rate down from 6% -> 1.2%.
- 14:15: revoked key K-89ab after 2-person verification (Dan Morris approval).
- 14:40: traffic normalized but WAF saw increased false positives due to strict geo-block rule; disabled geo-block and applied targeted IP blocklist.
- Post: opened JIRA:SRE-4123, assigned to Elliot for telemetry improvements and Maya for WAF rule hygiene.

Post-incident analysis checklist (to convert into a postmortem):
- [ ] Gather full request sample set for 14:00-15:00 UTC and store in secure S3 (retention 90d).
- [ ] Gather CDN/edge logs for same window (CDN request id mapping).
- [ ] Confirm root cause: key leak vs credential stuffing vs compromised partner. Evidence needed: key creation/last-used, any CI logs that printed keys, commit/PR scans.
- [ ] Validate detection thresholds and tune (reduce alert noise, ensure coverage of token spikes).
- [ ] WAF rules: move temporary rules into a labbed rule test run (2 days) before promoting.
- [ ] Customer outreach: template message drafted in /ops/templates/incident-key-leak.md.
- [ ] Security follow-up: rotate KMS keys if there's evidence of exfil.

Design notes / engineering gaps observed (brainstorm):
- We need per-key soft caps with automated notification + incremental throttles rather than all-or-nothing revokes.
- Improve client fingerprinting: stateless device fingerprint to group bot clusters and apply progressive rate limit.
- Add anomaly scoring (ML) using features: tokens/sec, distinct IPs, ASN diversity, user agent entropy, request timing autocorrelation.
- WAF rule lifecycle is manual; propose a sandboxed promotion flow and automated backout if FP > threshold.
- Add a fast-path CLI to issue temporary 1-hour keys for customers after rotation to reduce friction.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Should emergency throttle be per-region by default? (Pros: isolating blast radius; Cons: more config).
- What is our policy for notifying customers when we revoke keys for suspected abuse vs confirmed leak? (Legal/PR implications.)
- How aggressive should WAF blocks be for ML-inference endpoints where slight latency increases / altered headers can break clients?

Proposed action items (short-term):
- Elliot: instrument per-key daily p50/p95 token baselines + alerting (JIRA:SRE-4130).
- Maya: create WAF rule test harness and migration plan (JIRA:SEC-221).
- Priya: draft customer communication templates and emergency revocation SOP (JIRA:CS-198).
- Dan: evaluate adding automatic progressive throttles on ops edge (POC due 2026-04-15).

Audit trail and compliance notes:
- Any key revocation must be logged to audit.log with approver id. Ensure logs are immutable for 90d.
- When sampling full request payloads for investigation, follow the data-handling checklist: redact prompt text if it contains user PII, store in encrypted S3, and limit access.

Appendix: quick checklist for first 30m (one-page):
1) Identify top offending key(s) and top offending routes.
2) If >3 keys from same ASN: enable emergency throttle; sample logs.
3) If 1 key shows abuse: revoke and rotate; notify owner.
4) If WAF blocks legitimate traffic >2%: reduce WAF to monitor-only and apply manual IP blocks.
5) Open postmortem ticket and assign next steps.

Notes: this doc is a working draft — please comment inline on the runbook steps that require product/eng/legal signoff. We should move to an on-call handbook page once stabilized.

Related links and references:
- CONFLUENCE:infra/rate-limiter-policy (policy doc)
- JIRA:SRE-4123 (postmortem ticket)
- SLACK:#oncall-rotation (incident channel)
- GITHUB:github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter-config/pull/78 (current throttle config PR)

End of draft.
